controlName: Mechanisms for Tracking Identified Risks Over Time
purpose: Ensures identified AI risks aren't just recorded once and forgotten, but are actively tracked and reassessed as the system and its context evolve.
summary: Mechanisms for tracking identified AI risks over time are in place, ensuring risk trends are monitored, risks associated with high-priority AI system components are regularly reviewed, and measurable performance improvements or regressions are identified.
expectedStatementElements: What mechanism tracks identified risks over time (risk register, dashboard, ticketing system)
How often high-priority risks are reviewed and by whom
How the organization identifies when a risk trend is worsening versus improving
How tracked risk data feeds into decisions about whether treatment is working
evidenceExamples: AI risk register or tracking system with historical entries
Review cadence and log for high-priority risk items
Trend analysis showing risk levels over time
Documentation linking risk tracking data to treatment decisions
commonGaps: Risks are documented once during initial assessment and never revisited
No regular review cadence exists for high-priority risk items
No mechanism exists to detect whether a risk is trending better or worse over time
Risk tracking data isn't actually used to inform any decisions
interviewQuestions: Where do identified AI risks get tracked, and is that tracking still active or a one-time list?
How often are your highest-priority AI risks actually reviewed?
How would you know if a particular risk has been getting worse over the past six months?
Does anyone actually use the risk tracking data to make decisions, or does it just sit there?
